## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Kalyāṇadhammajātaka* (Ja 171) is a narrative discourse in the Pali *Jātaka* collection, rendered in English as *A Fine Reputation* [Fausböll 1879]. In the edited text of the *Jātaka*, the story opens with the verse incipit *Kalyāṇadhammo ti* [Fausböll 1879]. The narrative framework records that the Buddha related this story while staying at the Jetavana monastery near Sāvatthī, occasioned by the circumstances of a deaf mother-in-law (*badhirasassu*) and a devout, faithful householder (*kuṭumbī*) of Sāvatthī who had taken the three refuges and maintained the five precepts [Fausböll 1879].
